question: advisor said my stats class from my last school only counts as an elective not for my major. i dont get it, its the same class. can i ask for someone to look at it again

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're going through that. It's okay to not be okay, and you don't have to handle it alone.

Yes. If academic approval for a non-general education course equivalency has not yet been established and approved, the course may count as elective credit, but not toward a particular degree program. To have it evaluated for your major, contact the Convener of the appropriate program to review the course and its potential for transfer credit. If approved, the approval is sent to the Office of Admissions, which designates someone to update the appropriate systems. [2]

I don’t have verified information about how to identify your program’s Convener; the Office of the Provost may be able to help.

question: should i get an ipad or a laptop for college

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Ramapo publishes laptop recommendations, not an iPad-versus-laptop recommendation. Business students should invest in a Windows computer because many applications are only available for Windows. Students in the Susan and Nick Vallario School of Arts, Humanities, and Education may want to consider an Apple computer such as a MacBook, as many applications for this program are Mac-based. For other students, either a Windows or Mac laptop would be sufficient. Sciences, math, computer science, animation, video editing, and other computer-intensive majors should consider a computer meeting or exceeding the recommended “High-end” column. Ramapo does not recommend Chromebooks because they may not support the same applications as Windows and Mac laptops. Education discounts may be available; research options because vendor education pricing is not always lowest. [1][2]

Review Ramapo’s laptop recommendations: [https://www.ramapo.edu/its/student-laptop-recommendations/](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/student-laptop-recommendations/) [1][7]

For help deciding about a laptop purchase, contact the IT Help Desk. The published information doesn’t compare iPads with laptops or say who can advise specifically on that choice.

- **School of Arts, Humanities, and Education Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7365. Email: AHEOffice@ramapo.edu. Office: B-224. [31]
- **IT Help Desk**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: helpdesk@ramapo.edu. Location: 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [31]

I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Ramapo publishes laptop recommendations, not an iPad-versus-laptop recommendation. Business students should invest in a Windows computer because many applications are only available for Windows. Students in the Susan and Nick Vallario School of Arts, Humanities, and Education may want to consider an Apple computer such as a MacBook, as many applications for this program are Mac-based. For other students, either a Windows or Mac laptop would be sufficient. Sciences, math, computer science, animation, video editing, and other computer-intensive majors should consider a computer meeting or exceeding the recommended “High-end” column. Ramapo does not recommend Chromebooks because they may not support the same applications as Windows and Mac laptops. Education discounts may be available; research options because vendor education pricing is not always lowest. [1][2]

Review Ramapo’s laptop recommendations: [https://www.ramapo.edu/its/student-laptop-recommendations/](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/student-laptop-recommendations/) [1][7]

question: is it better to buy textbooks or rent them

body.answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Renting is usually cheaper if you only need the book for one course and don’t need to keep it. Buying can be better if you’ll reuse it, want to resell it, or need to write in it; compare the total rental cost and return rules with the used-book price.

Ramapo says students may choose to rent or buy books new or used; it doesn’t say which is better overall. Its Bookstore says renting can save up to 80% off the price of a new book. [15]

To find your required books, log into [web self-service](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/?name=homepage&accessibility=true), click “Student Services and Financial Aid,” select Registration, then “Buy Books Now from efollett.com.” This generates a list based on your current course registration status. You can pick up books at the bookstore or have them shipped to your home. [4]

The Bookstore also recommends ordering as early as possible to get USED copies and save money. [15]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [32]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/bookstore/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Buying can be better if you’ll reuse it, want to resell it, or need to write in it; compare the total rental cost and return rules with the used-book price.

Ramapo says students may choose to rent or buy books new or used; it doesn’t say which is better overall. Its Bookstore says renting can save up to 80% off the price of a new book. [15]

You can pick up books at the bookstore or have them shipped to your home. [4]

The Bookstore also recommends ordering as early as possible to get USED copies and save money. [15]

**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Start early and apply broadly: search job boards and company career pages, and tell professors, classmates, and family friends what kind of work you’re seeking. Tailor your résumé to each role, highlight class projects or other relevant experience, and practice a brief explanation of what you can contribute. Also consider research, part-time roles, and smaller organizations—these can build experience for future internships.

As a sophomore, update your resume and Handshake profile, then use Handshake to find summer internships and register for career events or schedule an appointment with the Career Center [1][2][12]. Attend career panels, workshops, and career fairs; connect with professionals through informational interviews and career programs; and consider job shadowing or employer information sessions [1]. Explore service-learning or volunteer learning opportunities and seek projects or leadership roles to build experience [1]. The Cahill Career Development Center can help with your search and provide Handshake and other job-search resources [6][7].

**Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [24]

Ramapo’s laptop recommendations say to use a MacBook for this program because many applications are Mac-based. For a Mac, the recommended options are a 13” MacBook Air or 14″ MacBook Pro, with MacOS 15 Sequoia, MacOS 26 Tahoe, or MacOS 27 Golden Gate; M3/M4 or higher; 16 GB or more RAM; and 512GB SSD.
